findings.title: zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes dict order matches input order
findings.body: nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids) returns a dict, and the code zips error_ids with events.values(). If get_multi omits missing keys or returns them in a different order than the input node_ids, the zip will associate error data with the wrong event IDs. The resulting ErrorEvent objects would have mismatched id/title/message/timestamp. A safer approach would be to iterate over zip(error_ids, node_ids) and look up each node_id in the returned dict explicitly.

findings.title: Mutual exclusivity validation uses truthiness, fails for age=0 or timestamp=0
findings.body: validate_timestamp checks `if self.initial_data.get("age")` and validate_age checks `if self.initial_data.get("timestamp")`. Since IntegerField allows 0 (timestamp has min_value=0, age has no min_value), a report with both age=0 and timestamp=123 would pass validation because `0` is falsy. The check should use `"age" in self.initial_data` or `self.initial_data.get("age") is not None` to correctly detect field presence.

findings.title: request.user.id may crash when authenticated via org auth token
findings.body: The analytics record call uses user_id=request.user.id unconditionally. When the request is authenticated with an org auth token (checked later via is_org_auth_token_auth), request.user may be None or an anonymous user without an id attribute. Since the analytics attribute is defined as required=False, the fix should be something like user_id=getattr(request.user, 'id', None) or a conditional check before accessing .id.

findings.title: TableWidgetVisualization rendered with hardcoded empty data behind feature flag
findings.body: When the 'use-table-widget-visualization' feature flag is enabled, the component renders TableWidgetVisualization with columns=[] and tableData containing empty data/meta. This means any table widget will appear completely empty when the flag is on, regardless of actual query results. The actual result.data, result.meta, fields, and other computed props are ignored. This appears to be placeholder/incomplete code that should not be merged in its current state.

findings.title: get_request_data mutates the input error_events list in-place
findings.body: error_events.sort(key=lambda x: x["timestamp"]) modifies the caller's list. While currently the list is request-scoped and used only once, this hidden side effect makes the function fragile: any future caller that reuses the list after calling get_request_data will observe an unexpectedly reordered sequence. Consider sorting a copy: sorted(error_events, key=...).

findings.title: get_recommended_event() called per issue inside PR comment generation loop
findings.body: get_environment_info calls issue.get_recommended_event() for each of the top issues (up to 5) during PR comment body construction. get_recommended_event typically hits nodestore/snuba and can be expensive. Since this runs inside get_comment_body which is called in a webhook/task context, the cumulative latency could be significant. Consider fetching environments in batch or caching the result.

findings.title: isLoading reports true during background refetches, not just initial load
findings.body: The hook sets isLoading: isFetching, which is true on every refetch (e.g., window focus, query key change), not only on the initial load. Consumers that show a full loading spinner based on isLoading will flash unnecessarily. Consider using isPending or isInitialLoading from useQuery, or exposing both isLoading and isFetching separately.
